newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to drop charges against ex-KGB agent.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to drop charges against ex-KGB agent.

text.p: The Justice Department said on Thursday it had decided to drop all charges against a former Soviet KGB agent who had been accused of conspiring to steal top secret information about the U.S. "Star Wars" defence programme.
In a brief interview, Deputy Attorney General Jamie Gorelick told Reuters the charges would be dropped in a case that has caused vigorous complaints from Moscow and warnings of retaliation.

Vladimir Galkin was accused of being a retired agent for the KGB who tried in 1991 to obtain secret reports and information about the Star Wars programme -- officially known as the Strategic Defence Initiative.
The 50-year-old former spy, who did not conceal his past occupation on a visa application, was arrested by FBI agents on Oct. 29 at John F. Kennedy airport in New York.
Justice Department officials said announcement that the charges were being dropped would be made at a court hearing, scheduled for 2 P.M.EST (1900 GMT), in Massachusetts for Galkin.

The officials said the CIA and the State Department initially supported bringing criminal charges against Galkin, but then changed their minds after Moscow threatened to retaliate and warned that relations with Washington could be affected.
